title: Hidden 'Obsidian 3' Model Tops Claude on Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0 Coding Benchmark
summary:
An unidentified AI agent listed as "Obsidian 3" recorded a 46.8% success rate on the FrontierCode 2.0 coding benchmark, outperforming the highest officially listed model, Claude Opus 5.5. The model uses a claude-code harness exclusive to Anthropic's models and carries a cost approximately 3.6 times higher than Opus 5.5 for equivalent effort, leading some analysts to suggest the model is an unreleased version of Anthropic's Fable family.

The private benchmark from Cognition consists of 132 tasks from real open-source repositories and grades models on whether their pull requests would actually be merged by a maintainer based on design judgment. Most frontier models struggled with the test's ambiguous prompts, with GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Terra recording a 42% success rate. Among open weights models, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash took the lead with a 28% score.

selectedTweets.bestBit: The result is a benchmark that is far from saturated, with the top model scoring just 45%.
selectedTweets.text:
Introducing FrontierCode 2.0: our new coding benchmark that measures a model’s ability to go beyond the spec.

Most coding evals measure a model’s ability to write code that meets a spec. With FrontierCode 1.0, we asked a new question: would you actually merge the PR?

FrontierCode 2.0 is comprised of more diverse tasks, featuring larger scopes and higher mergeability standards. We are now asking: not only would you merge this PR, but should you?

One key feature of FrontierCode 2.0 is underspecified prompts. Rather than including every engineering decision, prompts are deliberately ambiguous, giving the models room to demonstrate their judgment.

The result is a benchmark that is far from saturated, with the top model scoring just 45%.

selectedTweets.text:
Holy. Cognition has released FrontierCode 2.0, a tougher benchmark for AI coding agents. The results are brutal: Claude Opus 5.5 leads with just 45.5%, followed by GPT-6 Astra at 42.8%.

Even crazier, MORE thinking made Astra worse. On one bug, it passed 5/5 attempts at low reasoning but just 1/5 at maximum, where it deleted a public API.

Claude Opus 5.5 fixed another bug but failed ALL 25 attempts across five reasoning settings because it missed a critical cleanup requirement.

Even when AI fixes the bug, it can break the code around it.

selectedTweets.text:
FrontierCode 2.0 is the latest update of @cognition's private coding benchmark. Launched earlier today, it comprises 132 tasks in real open-source repositories, graded on whether a maintainer would merge the agent's change. An attempt that fails any blocking check scores 0, and the tasks stay private to avoid contamination. We run every task three times in Stirrup, our agentic harness.

Claude Opus 5.5 (max) leads at 46%, followed by GPT-6 Astra (max), GPT-6.1 Terra (max) and Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max), all at 42%. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max) is the highest-scoring open weights model at 28%, 18 points behind the leader.
